bibliography.abstract: Human curiosity and longing for the future have driven human progress from ancient times to the present. With the advancement of AI technology, human prediction algorithms have also drawn increasing attention from researchers. However, as AI technology continues to advance, we observe a counterintuitive phenomenon. Take human trajectory prediction algorithms as an example. Although models' quantitative prediction performance has improved, yielding one state-of-the-art model after another, the consideration of human behaviors, future thoughts, and social interactions themselves presents a gradually diminishing trend in the construction of these prediction algorithms, buried beneath numbers and metrics. In this manuscript, taking interactive art and human trajectory prediction algorithms as examples, we attempt to adopt a different analytical perspective to analyze the structural and developmental commonalities between these two fields. By examining specific interactive artworks and prediction algorithms, we aim to explore how human intuitions and art are associated with AI algorithms through three aspects, including perception, interaction, and timing, thereby providing new insights for the understanding and further research in this domain. We also observe an interesting phenomenon that certain art-inspired prediction algorithms can actually deduce intriguing patterns of human behaviors from the data, offering new potential avenues for understanding the relationship between human activities, state of The Art, and AI algorithms.
bibliography.title: From State of THE ART to Human Prediction Algorithms

orgs.label: Huazhong University of Science and Technology

en.what: The authors present a qualitative comparative analysis linking interactive art concepts with human trajectory prediction algorithms. By evaluating specific artworks and artificial intelligence models through the lenses of perception, interaction, and timing, the study demonstrates how incorporating artistic principles can uncover distinct patterns of human behavior within mobility data.
en.why: It exposes how recent trajectory algorithms prioritize raw benchmark scores while increasingly ignoring fundamental human behaviors and social dynamics, offering a conceptual framework to reintroduce human intuition into movement forecasting models.
